submitted.rationale: Index 1 (Fe 0.857, Sb 0.143; Sb-doped hematite) had the highest measured EQE, 0.228%. Index 0 (12% Sb) gave 0.141% and index 13 (FeSbO4, near 1:1) gave 0.018%. So the best films are Fe-rich hematite with a small amount of Sb, and the peak lies near 14% Sb.

rejected.reason: Measured EQE was only 0.018%, even though rutile FeSbO4 is stable (on the hull) with a ~2.1 eV gap.
Measured 0.141%, lower than index 1, so a little more Sb helps.
MACE puts it 0.18 eV/atom above the hull, and the measurements show EQE falling as Sb increases.

consultations.verdict: Support: rutile FeSbO4 is on the hull per MACE (0.002 eV/atom) and MEGNet HSE gap ~2.1 eV, well below the 3.2 eV photon energy, so a single-phase visible absorber is expected near Fe:Sb 1:1 (index 13).

Support for moving to the Fe-rich end: hematite Fe2O3 has a predicted HSE gap of ~2.8 eV, below the 3.2 eV photon energy, and Sb doping of hematite is a known way to raise conductivity. The Sb-rich FeSb2O4 phase is 0.18 eV/atom above the hull, so it is unlikely to form. That makes the Sb-rich side less attractive, and the 1:1 rutile phase gave low EQE.

Mildly supportive, mostly uninformative. The hematite gap stays below the 3.2 eV photon energy at every fidelity, so the most hematite-rich film should absorb well. The measured trend (0.018% at 49% Sb, 0.228% at 14% Sb) points toward the Fe-rich edge, so I am measuring index 0 (12% Sb).
